tasks.name: MSeries 01 — Apple Silicon kernel enhancements
tasks.prompt:
Run one focused kernel-maintenance pass for techmore/ElementaryOS_MSeries, prioritizing the J314S/T6000 M1 Pro and WD22TB4 display, USB4/hotplug and suspend reliability. Audit this prompt against current AGENTS.md, BRANCHING.md, latest relevant handoffs, open PRs and active work before proceeding. Reuse upstream-watch/dashboard #51, the newest successful kernel audit receipt and task memory; never create duplicate watchers.

1. Establish three distinct baselines: the published source in aurora/release.json; our exact source overlay/config in aurora/enhancements/series.json or unified72/series.json; and the running kernel. Read aurora/hardware-tests/README.md and later receipts, not just older table rows. If local access exists, record uname -r and brief passive DRM status. Kernel names alone do not bind image/module/DTB/boot-payload hashes. DRM HDMI/DP names do not identify the physical dock socket. Keep unknown identity or physical/visual acceptance unknown.

2. Discover current refs/releases and relevant PRs for omacom/linux-aurora, aurora-silicon/linux and confirmed contributor forks. Check AsahiLinux/linux, m1n1/U-Boot, Omacom hardware packages, and relevant Mesa/firmware changes at a scope justified by the selected candidate. Resolve moved repositories and paginate collections to completion. Record per-source coverage as refs-only, metadata, code-reviewed, unchanged with evidence, failed, or not checked. Never call ref discovery a full code review. Recheck PR merged/draft status and head SHA; old descriptions of PR #139 and the local 7.2.10 snapshot are historical, not current upstream status.

3. Use mseries/aurora/audit-upstream.py with the newest successful compatible --previous receipt and a unique scratch --output. It compares against release.json, not automatically the running overlay. Reuse unchanged immutable comparisons. Summarize large API responses and keep raw receipts in files. Treat compare/commit API caps explicitly; thousands of commits ahead are not thousands of reviewed fixes. Avoid cloning or reviewing the entire Linux history for a focused pass.

4. Rank at most five candidates and inspect one deeply. For each give immutable source URLs/SHAs, old-to-new baseline, intended benefit, hardware applicability, dependencies, evidence, risks/effort and IMPORT-CANDIDATE / AUDIT-DEEPER / WATCH / ALREADY-CARRIED / SKIP. Distinguish contributor claims from locally reproduced evidence. Before backporting, inspect both producer and consumer contracts in OUR source: e.g. PR #163's ENOSPC/EBUSY change cannot be transplanted blindly onto .20's older DCP routing contract. Check semantic equivalents and carried patches, not titles alone. PR #154 changes single-monitor bandwidth policy; document that tradeoff. Draft CPU context-loss diagnostics such as #170 are research, not proven deep sleep or safe maintenance trials.

5. Prepare at most one source/manifest/patch change only when evidence supports it. For source edits, use an isolated branch/worktree from origin/dev, preserve other work, verify actual SPDX/COPYING and attribution, pin source/config/checksums and run meaningful affected checks. Commit explicit paths, push and open/update a PR to dev; attach it. Do not merge. Research-only runs can retain a timestamped report/evidence outside the checkout and update task memory without a report-only PR. Never advance build pins from observed heads alone.

Preserve the running desktop and boot chain: no kernel installation/selection, boot.bin writes, boot arguments, display/audio/pairing changes, suspend/reboot/recovery experiments or panel/dock/compositor restarts. A new kernel version or successful build does not qualify J314S hardware, recovery, power savings or review parity. Never post to external upstreams or expose private logs/credentials. Honor deployment-coupled repository rules before pushing a component.

Audit the resulting report before finishing: verify counts/pagination, immutable citations and PR status, each adoption verdict against the correct baseline, and all claimed tests against receipts. Report limitations and unresolved gaps explicitly. Save durable memory with receipt paths and last-seen SHAs, clearly distinct from build pins. Finish with top findings, actions/artifacts/PR, checks versus claims, task-quality issues and one next iteration. Hand power measurements to task 02 through the report. Do not run task 02 or start another automation.

tasks.name: MSeries 02 — Power and performance optimization
tasks.prompt:
Run one focused power/performance maintenance pass for techmore/ElementaryOS_MSeries on the J314S/M1 Pro. Audit this prompt against current AGENTS.md, latest relevant handoffs, open/owned work and the previous successful power/kernel-task receipts. Read POWER-ROADMAP.md, power/README.md, power/AUDIT-2026-10-18.md, OPTIMIZATION.md, power/UPSTREAM.md, current compositor metrics and relevant video/kernel receipts. Treat dated opportunities, old task ownership and early unsupported-feature claims as history; later scoped evidence and actual running state take precedence.

Establish the actual kernel, running compositor and source/installed/loaded status first. The old Gala/Fairydust baseline is not the current Rust/.20-enh1 workload. Reuse upstream-watch and existing experiments; never create another watcher or repeat owned/completed AI/speech benchmarks. Read the dictation qualification ledger before work involving those resources. Take kernel candidates from task 01 rather than duplicating kernel import research.

Record measurement conditions: sensor name/path/units; charger-online AND battery status/signed flow; raw brightness/max; active output modes, scale/topology and fixed/variable selection; DPMS availability; governor/caps/profile; app/container activity and relevant pressure. Discover SMC Total System Power by chip/label, never a fixed hwmon index. Battery power_now is net flow and is not automatically total system power; charger connected can coexist with discharging. Never treat zero battery flow on AC as a zero-power machine. Missing sensors stay unknown. Preserve out-of-range brightness values (e.g. 503/500) as raw anomalies, not calibrated percentages or luminance.

Use brief passive samples for triage. Reuse existing sampler code, record its revision/hash, retain raw timed readings and state before/after, report n/duration/median/p10/p90 plus quantile method. Independently recompute summary statistics before accepting them. p10/p90 describe a sample distribution, not a confidence interval. Keep observer cost low: no frequent full /proc scans, concurrent builds/tracing or extra probes inside the window. Record any unavoidable observer activity. Per-process CPU can be sampled at endpoints with PID-start identity; distinguish one core=100% from aggregate CPU. CPU, IRQs, context switches and GPU jobs are activity indicators, not per-app watts or interchangeable wakeup counts.

If existing display_status.py loses mode/layout data because optional PowerSaveMode is missing, record modes separately and mark DPMS unknown. Do not weaken qualification by setting available=true without reviewing capture-session/qualification consumers and explicit completeness gates. A future tooling fix must test partial D-Bus capabilities and preserve hardware-acceptance boundaries. ALSA 'closed', RUNNING, unreadable and missing state are distinct; do not repeat the old always-running speaker claim from a stale snapshot.

Classify every run as observational, controlled baseline or paired experiment. Active desktop samples, different kernels/compositors, changed outputs, brightness, app load, power source or pending login changes cannot establish an optimization. Widely different uncontrolled windows must both be retained, not cherry-picked as before/after. Investigate measurement validity before attributing a change. Do not extrapolate battery runtime, idle floor or macOS parity from such samples. Historical macOS capture lacks active scenarios. Do not add separately measured savings into a claimed combined result.

Review current primary-source upstream evidence only where relevant to the selected opportunity; label each source's coverage. Confirm branch/path identity: imported Omacom diagnostics may live in a pinned feature branch and be absent from main; an empty main-branch history query is not proof of no updates. Check optimization-repo RESULTS.md and negative/void results. Preserve security/sandbox and speaker-safety constraints. Neither old browser flags nor a CPU profile label prove current decode or policy effectiveness.

Rank at most five opportunities by evidence, likely benefit (unknown when unmeasured), responsiveness/regression risk and effort. Prepare at most one justified reversible userspace source or measurement-tooling change. Use an isolated branch/worktree from origin/dev, preserve other work, run meaningful affected checks, commit explicit paths and open/update a PR to dev; attach it, do not merge. Honor deployment-coupled push rules. Research-only runs may retain timestamped report/evidence outside the checkout and update task memory without a report-only PR.

Controlled optimization claims require settled matched conditions, at least three alternating paired A/B trials, variability/uncertainty and latency/correctness checks. Present the exact hypothesis, controls, settling/exclusion rules, success criterion and rollback before an intervention. Existing refusal to close ChatGPT remains in force. This recurring task does not authorize closing apps, pausing services/containers, installing profiling packages, enabling tracing, changing brightness/refresh/DPMS/VRR, audio/speaker safety, power policy, boot/kernel state, suspend or reboot. Never weaken a browser sandbox to claim a power win. Passive inspection and source review can continue.

Audit the report against raw receipts: units/source semantics, statistics, comparable conditions, current-vs-historical claims and all claimed checks. Distinguish confirmed observations, hypotheses and untested benefits. Save durable task memory with evidence paths, conditions, negative results and the next focused step. End with findings, any source action/PR, checks/limits, prompt-quality issues and one next iteration. No automatic next-task launch, upstream posts or private credential/message/log disclosure.

Check elementary/os and Pantheon daily/beta sources, Ubuntu resolute packages, GTK/Granite/Gala/Wingpanel/Dock/Mutter/Smithay and Rust bindings, Mesa/PipeWire/WirePlumber/BlueZ, CodexBar, RepoBar, OpenCode, BlueFerry/Tether and other components actually pinned here. Preserve all local modifications and settings; follow CodexBar's merge-not-replace/schema/helper/account rules and the canonical complete dock/taskbar preparation. Compare package contents/dependencies and retain source/licenses/rollback artifacts. Do not run installers on the owner's desktop, publish apt/image releases or restart services. Report build success separately from installation and hardware acceptance. Kernel adoption belongs to task 01; this task owns userspace/package compatibility.
